For Server2, add a connection security rule.
For Server1, enable the File and Printer Sharing (Echo Request – ICMPv4-Out) firewall rule.
For Server1, add a connection security rule.

questions.explanation:
ICMP Echo Request traffic from `ping` arrives at Server2 as inbound traffic. Server2 must allow that inbound ICMPv4 traffic; enabling the built-in **File and Printer Sharing (Echo Request – ICMPv4-In)** firewall rule permits it. Windows Defender Firewall allows outbound traffic by default unless a blocking rule applies, so an outbound echo rule on Server1 is not the required first action.

**Learn more:** [Configure Firewall Rules With Group Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/network-security/windows-firewall/configure)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network has an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain containing 20 Active Directory sites. All user management is handled from a central site.  
  
You add users to a group and discover that the group changes do **not** appear on a domain controller at a remote site.  
  
You need to determine whether the group changes appear on other domain controllers.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
The Active Directory Replication Status Tool (ADREPLSTATUS) identifies and reports Active Directory replication errors for a single domain controller or for domain controllers throughout an Active Directory domain or forest. It is therefore suited to verifying whether group-membership changes have replicated to other domain controllers. Microsoft’s historical documentation describes this purpose, though the tool is no longer available for download.

**Learn more:** [How to get and use the Active Directory Replication Status Tool](https://learn.microsoft.com/fr-fr/previous-versions/troubleshoot/windows-server/get-use-active-directory-replication-status-tool) · [Troubleshooting Active Directory Replication Problems](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/manage/troubleshoot/Troubleshooting-Active-Directory-Replication-Problems)

Solution: Migrate SYSVOL from FRS to Distributed File System (DFS) Replication.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
Windows Server 2022 requires SYSVOL to use DFS Replication when promoting a replica domain controller. Migrating SYSVOL from FRS to DFS Replication removes the unsupported FRS dependency and allows the first Windows Server 2022 domain controller to be added.\
\
**Learn more:** [NTFRS deprecation blocks promotion of replica DCs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/active-directory/ntfrs-deprecation-blocks-replic-dc-installation) · [Migrate SYSVOL replication from FRS to DFS Replication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/storage/dfs-replication/migrate-sysvol-to-dfsr)

questions.question:
Solution: You upgrade the PDC emulator.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
A domain that replicates SYSVOL by using File Replication Service (FRS) must migrate SYSVOL replication to Distributed File System Replication (DFSR) before a newer Windows Server domain controller can be promoted. Upgrading the PDC emulator alone does not change SYSVOL replication from FRS to DFSR.\
\
**Learn more:** [Windows Server version 1709 no longer supports FRS](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/networking/windows-server-version-1709-no-longer-supports-frs) · [Migrate SYSVOL replication from FRS to DFS Replication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/storage/dfs-replication/migrate-sysvol-to-dfsr)

questions.domain: Migrate servers and workloads
questions.question:
Solution: You run the Active Directory Migration Tool (ADMT).  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
A domain using FRS for SYSVOL replication must be migrated to DFS Replication (DFSR) before a newer Windows Server domain controller can be promoted. ADMT migrates directory objects; it does not change SYSVOL replication from FRS to DFSR.\
\
**Learn more:** [Migrate SYSVOL replication from FRS to DFS Replication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/storage/dfs-replication/migrate-sysvol-to-dfsr) · [Windows Server version 1709 no longer supports FRS](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/networking/windows-server-version-1709-no-longer-supports-frs)

questions.question:
Solution: You raise both the domain and forest functional levels.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
Windows Server 2022 domain controllers cannot be added to a domain that uses File Replication Service (FRS) for SYSVOL replication. SYSVOL must first be migrated from FRS to Distributed File System Replication (DFSR); raising the domain and forest functional levels alone does not perform that migration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Windows Server version 1709 no longer supports FRS](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/networking/windows-server-version-1709-no-longer-supports-frs) · [Migrate SYSVOL replication from FRS to DFS Replication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/windows-server/storage/dfs-replication/migrate-sysvol-to-dfsr)

You have an Azure virtual machine named VM1. Crash dumps for a process named Process1 are enabled on VM1.  
  
When `process1.exe` on VM1 crashes, a technician must be able to access the memory dump files on the virtual machine. The technician must be prevented from accessing the virtual machine.  
  
To what should you grant the technician access?
questions.explanation:
Azure Diagnostics for Windows stores process crash dumps in a specified blob container in an Azure Storage account. Granting access to that Azure Blob Storage container lets the technician retrieve the dump files without granting access to VM1.\
\

questions.question:
You have 10 servers running Windows Server in a workgroup.  
  
You need to configure the servers so that all network traffic between them is encrypted. The solution must be as secure as possible.  
  
Which authentication method should you configure in a connection security rule?
questions.explanation:
Computer-certificate authentication provides strong mutual authentication for IPsec-protected traffic and does not depend on Active Directory domain membership. Kerberos V5 requires a domain, while a shared secret is less secure and harder to manage safely than certificate-based authentication.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set-NetIPsecRule (NetSecurity)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/netsecurity/set-netipsecrule?view=windowsserver2025-ps)

You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You need to configure a cloud witness for Cluster1.  
  
Which Azure Storage type should you use?

You have an Azure subscription containing a Log Analytics workspace named Workspace1.

questions.question:

Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel collects Windows Firewall application logs by using the Azure Monitor Agent (AMA) and its associated data collection rule; a data collection endpoint must be linked to that rule. Microsoft Integration Runtime is not a Windows Firewall log-collection agent and does not send those logs to Sentinel.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Sentinel data connectors reference — Windows Firewall Events via AMA](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/data-connectors-reference) · [Collect Windows Firewall logs with Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/vm/data-collection-firewall-logs)

questions.domain: Implement and manage Windows Server high availability

Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Azure Connected Machine agent enables Azure Arc management for an on-premises server, whereas Windows Firewall log collection for Microsoft Sentinel requires the Azure Monitor Agent configured through a data collection rule. Installing only the Connected Machine agent does not collect or send the firewall logs.\
\
**Learn more:** [Find your Microsoft Sentinel data connector](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/data-connectors-reference) · [Connect Microsoft Sentinel to other Microsoft services with a Windows agent-based data connector](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/connect-services-windows-based)

Does this meet the goal?

Windows Firewall log ingestion requires the relevant Microsoft Sentinel connector and monitoring-agent configuration on the Windows server; current Microsoft guidance identifies the Azure Monitor Agent as the mechanism for streaming Windows Firewall logs to the Sentinel workspace.\
\
**Learn more:** [Find your Microsoft Sentinel data connector](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/data-connectors-reference)

questions.domain: Monitor and troubleshoot Windows Server environments

Does this accomplish the goal?

A configured rule must collect the Windows Firewall logs and be associated with the server; agent installation alone does not enable that collection.\
\
**Learn more:** [Connect Microsoft Sentinel to other Microsoft services with a Windows agent-based data connector](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/connect-services-windows-based) · [Collect Windows Firewall logs from virtual machine with Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/vm/data-collection-firewall-logs)

Controlled folder access prevents untrusted applications from modifying files in protected folders and allows trusted or explicitly allowed applications to make changes. This meets the requirement to limit modification of protected-folder data to specific applications.\

Does this satisfy the goal?

Controlled Folder Access provides that capability by allowing trusted or explicitly allowed applications to modify files in protected folders.\
\
**Learn more:** [Protect security settings with tamper protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/prevent-changes-to-security-settings-with-tamper-protection) · [Configure controlled folder access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/controlled-folder-access-configure)

Does this satisfy the goal?

Controlled folder access is the Microsoft Defender feature that prevents untrusted applications from changing files in protected folders and supports an allow list for specified applications. Exploit protection instead applies exploit-mitigation techniques to processes and applications, so configuring it does not restrict modifications to protected folders to specified applications.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure controlled folder access (CFA)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/controlled-folder-access-configure) · [Create and deploy a Windows Defender Exploit Guard policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/configmgr/protect/deploy-use/create-deploy-exploit-guard-policy)

questions.domain: Secure Windows Server on-premises and hybrid infrastructures

Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Controlled Folder Access is the Microsoft Defender feature that prevents untrusted applications from changing files in protected folders and supports allowing specific applications to make those changes. Reputation-based protection does not configure protected folders or the allowed applications list, so it cannot enforce this requirement. [Configure controlled folder access (CFA) — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/controlled-folder-access-configure)\

**Learn more:** [Configure controlled folder access (CFA) — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/controlled-folder-access-configure)

questions.domain: Implement Disaster Recovery
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A server named Server1 runs Windows Server 2022 and belongs to a three-node failover cluster.  
  
You need to upgrade Server1 to Windows Server 2025 while minimizing downtime for the cluster.  
  
What should you do first?

Update the functional level of the cluster.

questions.explanation:
A rolling cluster OS upgrade transfers clustered workloads off the node being upgraded by pausing it and draining its roles to the other cluster nodes. This maintains cluster availability while Server1 is upgraded. Eviction is optional after draining for a clean installation, and the cluster functional level is updated only after every node runs the newer operating system.

**Learn more:** [Upgrade a Windows Server failover cluster with a cluster OS rolling upgrade](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/failover-clustering/cluster-operating-system-rolling-upgrade)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network has an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) forest.  
  
You need to deploy a converged Storage Spaces Direct infrastructure. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Use an Ethernet fabric.  
- Remove the requirement for Data Center Bridging (DCB).  
  
Which Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) networking technology should you implement?
questions.explanation:
iWARP provides RDMA over TCP/IP on Ethernet, so it uses TCP reliability and does not require a lossless Ethernet fabric or Data Center Bridging. RoCEv1 and RoCEv2 generally require lossless Ethernet configuration, while InfiniBand is not an Ethernet fabric. Microsoft identifies iWARP and RoCE as RDMA options for Storage Spaces Direct, with iWARP being simpler to configure.

Server4 has the following IP configuration:  
  
```text  
Ethernet adapter Ethernet:  
Connection-specific DNS Suffix . . :  
IPv4 Address . . . . . . . . . . . : 192.168.0.10  
Subnet Mask . . . . . . . . . . . : 255.255.255.0  
Default Gateway . . . . . . . . . : 192.168.0.1
```  

From Server4, you can successfully ping Server1 and Server2. When you ping Server3, you receive a **Request timed out** response.

A misconfiguration of which component on Server3 can cause the **Request timed out** response?
questions.explanation:
A subnet mask determines whether a destination is considered local or remote. An incorrect, overly restrictive subnet mask on Server3 can treat Server2 as local while treating Server4 as remote, causing Server3 to send its ICMP reply through routing rather than directly to Server4. This produces the observed asymmetric connectivity. DNS is not used when pinging IP addresses, and a default-gateway problem would not prevent communication with another host Server3 considers local.

options.text: Add an additional Site-to-Site VPN between the on-premises network and Vnet1.
Add a private endpoint to Subnet2.
To Subnet2, add a route table that contains a user-defined route.
Update the routing information on the on-premises routers.

questions.explanation:
Without BGP, VPN route exchange is not dynamic. When a VNet address range is extended, the on-premises routers need routing information for that new prefix so they forward traffic for Subnet2 through the existing Site-to-Site VPN. Azure VPN Gateway documentation states that BGP exchanges routes between the VPN gateway and the on-premises VPN device; without it, the required route must be configured on the on-premises side.

You are troubleshooting SYSVOL replication problems on DC1.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a server named Server1 running Windows Server 2019 with the Hyper-V server role installed. Server1 hosts the virtual machines shown in the following table.

Which virtual machines can you import into Server2?

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Windows Server Failover Cluster (WSFC) containing three nodes. Each node is running Windows Server 2022.

You need to assess the cluster's status in preparation for the rolling upgrades. The solution must meet these requirements:

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to satisfy the technical requirements for Share1.

questions.explanation:
The requirement for Share1 is to control storage consumption and/or the types of files users can store on the share, which is exactly what File Server Resource Manager (FSRM) provides through quota management (limit space per folder/volume) and file screening (block specified file types such as media files). Storage Migration Service is for migrating servers/shares to a new server, Storage Replica provides block-level volume replication for disaster recovery, and Server Manager alone doesn't offer quota or file-screening policy - none of these satisfy a quota/file-screen requirement. lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have two on-premises Hyper-V hosts named Server1 and Server2. Server1 hosts two virtual machines named VM1 and VM2. Server2 hosts three virtual machines named VM21, VM22, and VM23.  
  
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to use Azure Site Recovery to replicate every virtual machine to Azure.  
  
You need to deploy the Microsoft Azure Site Recovery Provider in the on-premises infrastructure.  
  
What is the minimum number of providers that you must install?

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an on-premises Windows Server named Server1. Server1 hosts multiple file shares and has an IP address of 192.168.10.12.  
  
You have an Azure subscription.

What should the solution include?

Solution: You turn off Windows Defender Firewall on Server1.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Migrate and Modernize does not support teamed NICs for physical-server migration. Disabling Windows Defender Firewall does not address the enabled NIC Teaming configuration, so it does not make the server eligible for migration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Support matrix for migration of physical servers, AWS VMs, and GCP VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/migrate/migrate-support-matrix-physical-migration?view=migrate-classic)

questions.question:
Proposed solution: Shrink the data disk on Server1.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Migrate physical-server migration supports data disks up to 32 TB, so a 3-TB data disk does not require reduction. Teamed NICs are unsupported; because NIC Teaming remains enabled, shrinking the disk does not satisfy the migration requirements.\
\
**Learn more:** [Support matrix for migration of physical servers, AWS VMs, and GCP VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/migrate/migrate-support-matrix-physical-migration?view=migrate-classic)

questions.domain: Migrate servers and workloads
questions.question:
Solution: Disable NIC Teaming on Server1.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Migrate’s agent-based physical-server migration does not support teamed NICs. Disabling NIC Teaming removes that unsupported configuration, allowing the server to meet this migration requirement.\
\
**Learn more:** [Support for physical server migration in Azure Migrate and Modernize](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/migrate/migrate-support-matrix-physical-migration?view=migrate-classic)

questions.question:
Solution: You turn off Microsoft Defender Antivirus on Server1.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
NIC teaming on a replicated physical server is unsupported for Azure Site Recovery–based physical-server replication, which Azure Migrate uses for agent-based physical-server migration. Disabling antivirus software does not address that unsupported network configuration, so it is insufficient to make the server eligible for migration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Support matrix for disaster recovery of VMware VMs and physical servers to Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/site-recovery/vmware-physical-azure-support-matrix) · [Support for physical server migration in Azure Migrate and Modernize](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/migrate/migrate-support-matrix-physical-migration)

With immediate failback allowed, preventing App1 from moving back to Server1 requires a failback configuration that prevents or defers failback.\

Setting Server2 as the highest preferred owner keeps App1 on Server2 when Server1 restarts. Microsoft documents that the preferred-owner list is ordered by preference and that allowed failback returns a role to its preferred owner.\

questions.explanation:
With automatic failback enabled, a clustered role can fail back to its preferred owner when that owner returns online. Setting Server2 as the highest-priority preferred owner makes Server2 the preferred location for App1, so App1 remains on Server2 when Server1 starts. Preferred-owner order controls the preferred ownership of a clustered role.\

From the Enable Replication wizard, configure recovery points.
From the Properties of VM1, enable automatic checkpoints.
From the Enable Replication wizard, modify the replication frequency.

questions.explanation:
Hyper-V Replica uses additional hourly recovery points to retain earlier replica states. Configuring recovery points in the Enable Replication wizard allows recovery to a prior point in time, including one within the past eight hours.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a server named Server1 that runs Windows Server with the Hyper-V server role installed. You also have a Hyper-V failover cluster named Cluster1. All servers belong to the same domain.  
  
You need to make sure that Hyper-V Replica uses Kerberos authentication on the default port to replicate virtual machines from Cluster1 to Server1.  
  
What should you do on Server1?

options.text: Add primary servers to the Hyper-V Replica Broker configuration.
From Hyper-V Settings, select Enable incoming and outgoing live migrations.
From Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security, enable the Hyper-V Replica HTTPS Listener (TCP-In) rule.
From Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security, enable the Hyper-V Replica HTTP Listener (TCP-In) rule.

questions.explanation:
Hyper-V Replica with Kerberos authentication uses HTTP over the default TCP port 80. The replica destination must allow this inbound traffic by enabling the **Hyper-V Replica HTTP Listener (TCP-In)** Windows Defender Firewall rule. HTTPS is used for certificate-based authentication.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network includes an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain. Microsoft Defender Credential Guard with UEFI lock is configured on every domain member.  
  
Within the domain, you deploy a Windows Server computer named Server1 and disable Credential Guard on Server1.  
  
You need to ensure that Server1 is **not** subject to Credential Guard restrictions.  
  
What should you do next?

options.text: Disable the Turn on Virtualization Based Security group policy setting.
Run dism and specify the /Disable-Feature and /FeatureName:IsolatedUserMode parameters.
Run the Device Guard and Credential Guard hardware readiness tool.

questions.explanation:
Credential Guard configured with UEFI lock stores its protection state in EFI firmware variables, so merely disabling the related Group Policy setting or an operating-system feature does not fully remove the restrictions. The Device Guard and Credential Guard hardware readiness tool supports disabling Credential Guard and performs the UEFI-lock removal workflow, which requires confirmation during startup.

**Learn more:** [Configure Credential Guard](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-za/windows/security/identity-protection/credential-guard/configure)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing a virtual machine named VM1 that runs Windows Server and is located in the East US Azure region. The subscription includes the storage accounts shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783879383882-mpfgx9oe.png)  
  
You plan to configure Diagnostic settings for VM1.  
  
Which storage accounts should you specify for these settings?
questions.explanation:
A storage account used for VM diagnostics/boot diagnostics must be a standard general-purpose account located in the same region and subscription as the VM. VM1 is in East US, so only East US accounts qualify. storage1 is a Standard general-purpose v2 account in East US and is valid. storage2 (BlockBlobStorage) and storage3 (FileStorage) are premium, specialized accounts and are not supported for diagnostics (premium storage returns a StorageAccountTypeNotSupported error and these kinds don't provide the required blob/table endpoints). storage4 is StorageV2 but located in Central US, the wrong region. Therefore only storage1 can be specified.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network includes an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) forest. The forest has a user named User1.  
  
You deploy a read-only domain controller (RODC) called RODC1.  
  
You need to make sure that User1 is a local administrator on RODC1. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network contains an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain named contoso.com. The domain was created by using domain controllers running Windows Server 2022.  
  
You plan to deploy a custom app. The app requires a domain controller that runs an older version of Windows Server.  
  
What is the oldest Windows Server version that you can use for the domain controller in contoso.com?
questions.explanation:
Windows Server 2022 domains use the Windows Server 2016 functional level, the most recent AD DS functional level. That functional level supports domain controllers running Windows Server 2016, Windows Server 2019, and Windows Server 2022; it does not support Windows Server 2012 R2. Thus, Windows Server 2016 is the oldest compatible choice.

You need to onboard the servers to Microsoft Sentinel while minimizing administrative effort.  
  
What should you use to onboard the servers to Microsoft Sentinel?

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A network contains an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain with 10,000 users.  
  
You plan to move the domain to a new forest.  
  
You must ensure that users can sign in to the new forest by using their current passwords. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Migrate the users by running ldifde.exe.
Migrate the users by using the Active Directory Administrative Center.
Migrate the users by using the Active Directory Migration Tool (ADMT).
Create Password Settings Objects (PSOs) in the new forest.

After the restart, this error message appears: "Boot failure. Reboot and Select proper Boot Device or Insert Boot Media in selected Boot Device."

You plan to deploy a new line-of-business (LOB) application on VM1.  
  
You need to ensure that the application can create child processes.  
  
What should you configure on VM1?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender Exploit Protection provides the app-level **Don't allow child processes** mitigation. When enabled, it prevents an application from creating child processes; therefore, configure Exploit protection so that this mitigation does not block the LOB application.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an on-premises server named Server1 running Windows Server with the Hyper-V server role installed.

You plan to back up Server1 to Azure by using Azure Backup.  
  
Which two Azure Backup options require deployment of Microsoft Azure Backup Server (MABS)? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Azure Backup Server provides bare-metal recovery protection and supports backup of Hyper-V virtual machines. Files and folders and System State can instead be backed up directly to Azure by using the Microsoft Azure Recovery Services agent.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a server running Windows Server. It is configured to encrypt all inbound traffic by using a connection security rule.

Generation 1 and the supported 8.0 VM configuration version remain part of the imported VM configuration; an import does not itself upgrade that version. A Hyper-V virtual switch is host-specific, so VNet1 is not preserved on Server2 unless a compatible switch is separately configured there.

**Learn more:** [Upgrade virtual machine version in Hyper-V on Windows or Windows Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/virtualization/hyper-v/deploy/upgrade-virtual-machine-version-in-hyper-v-on-windows-or-windows-server) · [Export and import virtual machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/virtualization/hyper-v/deploy/export-and-import-virtual-machines)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network has an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain that includes two servers, Server1 and Server2, running Windows Server.  
  
You need to make sure that the Computer Management console can be used to manage Server2. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which two Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security rules should be enabled on Server2? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.

options.text: all the rules in the Remote Event Log Management group

questions.explanation:

It also requires the Remote Event Log Management firewall exceptions, including the named-pipe, RPC, and RPC endpoint-mapper rules; enabling the **Remote Event Log Management** group provides those related exceptions with the smallest applicable group-level selection.

You have an Azure subscription that contains a virtual machine named VM1. VM1 runs Windows Server and uses Azure Disk Encryption.  
  
You need to determine which Azure key vault contains the encryption keys for VM1. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
Which PowerShell cmdlet should you run?
questions.explanation:
`Get-AzVMDiskEncryptionStatus` returns the encryption status for a virtual machine and includes the encryption-secret URL, key-encryption-key URL, and the resource IDs of the Key Vaults containing the relevant keys. This directly identifies the key vault associated with Azure Disk Encryption for the VM.\
\
**Learn more:** [Get-AzVMDiskEncryptionStatus (Az.Compute)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.compute/get-azvmdiskencryptionstatus?view=azps-14.6.0)

You are planning a data-share migration to support the on-premises migration plan.  
  
What should you use to carry out the migration?
questions.explanation:

You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You need to onboard Server1 into Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
What should be installed on Server1?

options.text: the Microsoft Entra provisioning agentD. the Azure Connected Machine agent

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an on-premises Windows Server computer named Server1 that hosts a shared folder named Share1.  
  
You deploy a new virtual machine named Server2.  
  
You need to migrate Share1 to Server2. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Ensure users can access the UNC path `\server1\share1` after Server1 is decommissioned.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you use for the migration?
questions.explanation:
Storage Migration Service transfers files, file shares, and security configuration to a destination server. Its optional cutover lets the destination assume the source server’s identity, so users can continue accessing the existing `\\server1\share1` path after the original server is decommissioned.

**Learn more:** [Storage Migration Service overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/storage/storage-migration-service/overview) · [Use Storage Migration Service to migrate a server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/storage/storage-migration-service/migrate-data)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are planning the deployment of Microsoft Sentinel.  
  
Which type of Microsoft Sentinel data connector should you use to meet the security requirements?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Identity monitors on-premises Active Directory Domain Services by analyzing domain controller traffic and events to detect identity-based threats such as reconnaissance, compromised credentials, lateral movement, and domain dominance attacks. Connecting the Microsoft Defender for Identity data connector to Microsoft Sentinel streams these alerts and signals into Sentinel, enabling detection and investigation of on-premises identity attacks—something the Azure AD, Defender for Cloud, or Threat Intelligence - TAXII connectors do not provide, as those focus on cloud identity sign-ins, cloud workload protection, and external threat intelligence feeds respectively.

Enable Azure Arc on each managed server.
From Server1, run the Set-AzWebApp cmdlet.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have two on-premises Windows Server computers named Server1 and Server2. Server2 hosts a Hyper-V virtual machine named VM1.  
  
You have an Azure subscription containing a Recovery Services vault.  
  
You need to configure Azure Site Recovery to replicate workloads from the on-premises environment to Azure.  
  
What should you do initially?

options.text: On VM1, run the AzureSiteRecoveryProvider.exe command.
On VM1, run the AzureBackupAgentInstaller.exe command.
On Server2, run the AzureBackupAgentInstaller.exe command.
On Server2, run the AzureSiteRecoveryProvider.exe command.

questions.explanation:
For Hyper-V replication to Azure, the Azure Site Recovery Provider must be installed on every Hyper-V host that will be added to the Hyper-V site, including Server2. The provider registers the host with the Recovery Services vault and enables Site Recovery to obtain host metadata. The Azure Backup agent is not the required initial deployment component for this configuration.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network includes an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) forest. The forest has a user named User1.  
  
You deploy a read-only domain controller (RODC) named RODC1.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your on-premises network has an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain. The domain includes 100 Windows Server servers that are Azure Arc-enabled.  
  
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You need to automatically change the password for the built-in local administrator account on every computer in the domain. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- The password must be changed automatically every 30 days.  
- Administrative effort must be minimized.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: Windows Local Administrator Password Solution (Windows LAPS)

questions.explanation:
Windows Local Administrator Password Solution (Windows LAPS) centrally manages the password for a local administrator account on Active Directory-joined Windows devices and regularly rotates it. Its `PasswordAgeDays` policy controls the maximum password age and defaults to 30 days, enabling automated rotation with minimal administration.

**Learn more:** [Windows LAPS overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/windows-server/identity/laps/laps-overview) · [Configure policy settings for Windows LAPS](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/laps/laps-management-policy-settings)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have two servers, Server1 and Server2, running Windows Server.  
  
You perform the following actions:  
  
- On Server1, you create an Application Control policy named Policy1 that includes a rule allowing all executables in the `D:\Folder1` folder.  
- You add a rule to Policy1 that trusts the `\Server2\Folder2` folder.  
- You deploy Policy1.  
  
You need to confirm that Policy1 is applied to Server1.  
  
Which Event Viewer log should you review?

options.text: Applications and Services Logs\Microsoft\Windows\AppLocker\MSI and Script

questions.explanation:
The CodeIntegrity Operational log contains Application Control policy activation events and events related to the control of executables, DLLs, and drivers. It is therefore the relevant Event Viewer log for confirming deployment of an executable Application Control policy.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Hyper-V host named Server1 that runs Windows Server. Server1 hosts a virtual machine named VM1, which runs Windows Server and contains multiple file shares.  
  
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You need to migrate the file shares to Azure Storage by using Azure Storage Mover. The solution must minimize downtime and administrative effort.  
  
What should you do first on the on-premises network?

options.text: On Server1, install the Azure Connected Machine agent.
On VM1, install the Azure Storage Mover agent.
On VM1, install the Azure Connected Machine agent.
On Server1, install the Azure Storage Mover agent.

questions.explanation:
Azure Storage Mover uses a dedicated, VM-based migration agent appliance that runs on a supported Hyper-V or VMware host and is ideally deployed close to the source storage. Deploying the Storage Mover agent on the Hyper-V host provides access to the file-share source while avoiding changes to the workload VM and enabling migration jobs to be managed through Azure.

**Learn more:** [Deploy an Azure Storage Mover agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage-mover/agent-deploy)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription containing a virtual machine named Server1.  
  
Server1 cannot start and shows this message: “Getting Windows ready. Don’t turn off your computer.”  
  
You must submit an Azure support ticket and attach Server1’s memory dump.  
  
Which file from Server1 should you attach?
questions.explanation:
Windows stores the operating-system memory dump at `%SystemRoot%\\MEMORY.DMP`; when the Windows system drive is `C:`, the file is `C:\\Windows\\Memory.dmp`. Microsoft’s Azure VM guidance directs support cases to locate `Memory.dmp` in the attached OS disk’s Windows folder and attach it to the ticket.\
\
**Learn more:** [Collect an OS memory dump file for Azure support](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/azure/virtual-machines/windows/collect-os-memory-dump-file)
